supersededForGapTruth.statement: SUPERSEDED FOR GAP TRUTH. This file is no longer authoritative for WHICH scenarios are Traceability Gaps, which test cases are unclaimed, or how many links of each kind exist. That is now derived, in one place, by scripts/verification/reconcile-traceability.ts into docs/verification/traceability-map.json, which 003 §Section 1 makes the aggregate that owns gap truth in both directions. Task 06's `counts` block and its gap MEMBERSHIP lists were removed here so two artefacts can never disagree.
supersededForGapTruth.whatThisFileStillOwns: The prose the map cannot derive: WHY each gap is a gap (`gapRationales`), WHICH clause of a partially covered scenario is still unproven (`partialCoverageRationales`), the reviewed quarantine-adjacent candidates and the reasoning that none was committed (`quarantineReport`), the classification of the deliberately unannotated cases (`outOfScopeTestCases`), and task 06's before/after suite baseline. Membership in every one of those lists is re-derived by the map; if a rationale here names a scenario the map no longer reports as a gap, the map is right and this rationale is stale.

reconciledAtGeneration.note: Every count task 06 measured was reproduced independently by the task 07 reconciler from the register, the deduplicated sink and the runner's executed-test inventory. No figure was adjusted to match.

policy: ANNEX, NOT A LEDGER. Originally task 06's gap ledger, written here because docs/verification/scenario-register.json mechanically rejects extra fields: `serializeRegister` in scripts/verification/register-scenarios.ts emits a fixed key set and drops everything else, and register-scenarios.test.ts pins `serializeRegister(regenerated) === committedRaw()` byte for byte. That constraint still holds and the register is still byte-unchanged. Task 07 resolved the open architect question the other way round: the gap ledger was NOT folded into the register, because 003 §Section 1 gives gap truth to the derived Traceability Map, not to the identity store. See `supersededForGapTruth`.

gapRationales.heading: Should produce one admitted outcome when a candidate satisfies the Admission Gate
gapRationales.reason: No case in the EAP corpus asserts the CARDINALITY the scenario names — exactly one admitted Admission Decision for one satisfying candidate. Admission is exercised throughout as a precondition of other flows, never as its own subject.

gapRationales.heading: Should return the same verdict when identical candidate evidence is submitted by a hostile identity
gapRationales.reason: No case submits identical candidate content twice under different identities and compares the verdicts. Determinism-under-hostile-identity is untested.

gapRationales.heading: Should reject HorizonId when it is empty
gapRationales.reason: `createHorizonId` is imported by packages/graph-core/test/eap-types.test.ts and never called. The empty-HorizonId refusal IS exercised at the MCP boundary (MALFORMED_CONTRACT, in eap-conformance and eap-mcp-contract), but that is the transport contract, not the value-object constructor this scenario is stated over — so a link would misattribute the proof.

gapRationales.heading: Should preserve HorizonId opacity when topology changes
gapRationales.reason: No case re-reads a HorizonId after its Horizon gains a declared parent to show the identifier is unchanged and encodes no topology.

gapRationales.heading: Should prevent admission or Relative Authority when a Negotiation Seed carries them
gapRationales.reason: `validateNegotiationSeed` is imported by packages/graph-core/test/eap-types.test.ts and never called. Nothing attaches admission or authority to a seed and observes the rejection.

gapRationales.heading: Should commit a Changeset atomically when incremental and final gates accept it
gapRationales.reason: Exercised by packages/mcp-server/test/commit-atomic.test.ts, which lies OUTSIDE the 21-file EAP corpus task 06 annotates. A gap in the annotated set, not necessarily in the suite. Extending annotation to the changeset corpus is a scope decision for the architect.

gapRationales.heading: Should leave no durable mutation when a Changeset gate refuses it
gapRationales.reason: Same as EAP-SVCS-001: the changeset gate suite is outside the annotated EAP corpus.

gapRationales.heading: Should remain immutable when a consumer handles a governed event
gapRationales.reason: No case takes an emitted governed event, attempts to mutate it, and shows the mutation grants no permission to change host state.

gapRationales.heading: Should isolate Claim Snapshot Store results when tenants use the same CellKey
gapRationales.reason: Exercised by packages/mcp-server/test/tenant-isolation.test.ts, outside the annotated EAP corpus. Cross-tenant isolation IS partially covered inside the corpus (EAP-SEC-001), but over contestation targets rather than the Claim Snapshot Store this scenario names.

gapRationales.heading: Should return no Horizon when HorizonId does not exist
gapRationales.reason: packages/mcp-server/test/horizon-durability.test.ts calls `HorizonStore.get` only for a horizon it just created. The empty result for an absent id — 'without inventing a root or parent' — is never asserted.

gapRationales.heading: Should return Admission Decisions in Sequence order when historySince matches records
gapRationales.reason: `AdmissionLedgerStore` is constructed in horizon-durability.test.ts but `historySince` is called by no test in the repository.

gapRationales.heading: Should run MCP host contract flows when no LLM provider is configured
gapRationales.reason: Every host contract flow in the corpus in fact runs without an LLM provider, but no case ASSERTS the absence of an LLM dependency or credential. The property holds incidentally; nothing would fail if it stopped holding, so there is nothing to bind.

gapRationales.heading: Should keep the deterministic MCP host independent when an LLM response is malicious
gapRationales.reason: No case feeds prompt-injected content through the client adapter and shows the host treats it as untrusted proposal input. The adapter's local guards (token, evidence) are tested but are a different obligation.

partialCoverageRationales.note: 003 §Section 2: a `covers-partially` link alone can never promote a scenario to `evidenced`. These 24 are therefore NOT evidenced by this corpus; each is listed so task 09 reports them as unpromoted with a reason rather than as silent absences. `partialLinks` is the number of partial links.

`HorizonBudgetExhausted` is never read back — only the escalation outcome and its reason.
'exactly one' Refusal, and the explicit client obligation on it.

All four links are producing-side (an allocator never emits a decreasing Sequence). `createSequence` and `validateSequenceAdvance` are imported by eap-types.test.ts and never called, so the REJECTION the scenario states is untested.
All three prove the converse — every listed code HAS an obligation. Constructing a Refusal from an unmapped code and observing the failure is untested.
`HorizonInitiated` and its seedRef/budgetRef payload.
`PersistentDeltaAdmitted` and the recorded Sequence.
No single case pairs 'KnowledgeContested is recorded' with 'the target claims are not directly edited or deleted'; the corpus splits the two clauses across cases.
The append-only audit reference for the reversible path.
`CapabilityExecuted` is never read back; only the consumed flag and the reuse refusal.
No case runs `AssessConformance` or produces independent host and client verdicts. The two files NAMED eap-conformance report exclusions and adapter invariants instead.
Only `TruthOwnershipSuspended` of the eleven governed events the scenario enumerates has its minimum payload checked.
Every link observes a restart or a rebuild over recall/promotion state, never the claims + ownership + Sequence triple the scenario states.
The Given is a corrupt `refs` column, not the 'no registered reverse-dependency edges' the scenario states.
The client obligation on the refusal is never read back, and three of the four links arise from corrupt durable state rather than a violated host rule.
The MCP client is a stub; 'only the deterministic MCP host may admit or persist it' is unexercised.
Atomic commit is shown; the monotonic Sequence advance and the observable event are not.
No single link performs the scenario's whole When — Recall requested, interrupted, THEN resumed — with all three Then clauses. The six links each carry one fragment.
`CapabilityExecuted` is not read back in either link.
Two links are client-adapter-side; the host-side link never verifies that no mutation occurred.
No link pairs the absent-resource outcome with the 'without leaking another tenant's state' clause in the same case.
'approval does not waive evidence requirements' is asserted by none of the five.
The scenario's Given spans an invalid CellKey, an empty HorizonId AND a cross-tenant identifier; the corpus splits these across three cases and covers no CellKey arm at a governed boundary.
The single link replays a COMMAND. The scenario's Given is a captured EVENT (`KnowledgeVerified`, `PromotionProposed`, `CapabilityExecuted`) replayed as though it were a command — untested.

reviewedCandidates.subject: Destination status of an indirect dependent in a Recall cascade.
tests: packages/mcp-server/test/f001-retry6-readmodel-and-freshness.test.ts :: truth-ownership suspension reaches the `authority` table, and indirect dependents stay deferred
packages/mcp-server/test/f001-retry7-closure-gate.test.ts :: an indirect dependent may still be CONCRETIZEd but is refused at VERIFY
packages/mcp-server/test/f001-retry7-closure-gate.test.ts :: a verified candidate that a later recall pulled into its closure cannot be promoted
packages/mcp-server/test/f001-retry8-resume-index.test.ts :: resuming to completion does NOT clear the gate: the closure is still closed (003 defers the exit)
reviewedCandidates.verdict: NOT a violation, binding not committed. Each case asserts that the destination status stays UNDECIDED — the read model invents no status and the lifecycle is held short of `verified`. They keep QA2 open rather than resolving it, which is the opposite of discharging it. Left unannotated with an in-file comment naming the family.

reviewedCandidates.subject: Mapping a LegacyClaimStatus value into the Epistemic Lifecycle.
tests: packages/graph-core/test/eap-types.test.ts :: Should explicitly prevent inferred mapping of LegacyClaimStatus
reviewedCandidates.verdict: NOT a violation, binding not committed. The case asserts the mapper THROWS with the deferral reason — it pins the ambiguity open. Left unannotated with an in-file comment naming the family.

reviewedCandidates.subject: Page size, batching limits and completion bounds for very large reverse-dependency closures.
tests: packages/mcp-server/test/f001-retry7-closure-gate.test.ts :: exhausting the batch cap is reported distinctly instead of looking like completion
packages/mcp-server/test/f001-retry7-closure-gate.test.ts :: a completed recall reports complete:true and no batch-limit signal
packages/mcp-server/test/f001-retry8-resume-index.test.ts :: re-driving a batch-cap-exhausted case finishes it and reports it as resumed
reviewedCandidates.verdict: NOT a violation. No case asserts a maximum batch size, page size or completion bound: each forces `RECALL_LIMITS.maxBatches` to an explicit test value and checks only the REPORTING shape, restoring the original afterwards. The third is bound to EAP-RECL-003 (resume semantics), not to any bound. Flagged so task 08 can re-check the reasoning rather than take it on trust.
